summary: CLI exfiltrates host identifiers and user-typed credentials to a hardcoded author-controlled Google Apps Script endpoint
details: On every invocation, bin/index.js gates behind an auth prompt that collects the user-typed Employee ID and password together with host and network identifiers — public IP, geolocation (city/region/country/postal/latitude/longitude), ISP, OS, hostname, username, CPU/RAM/arch, editor identity, and current working directory/project name — and sends them as query parameters to a hardcoded Google Apps Script URL (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbw.../exec), with IP/geo lookups via ipwho.is and ip-api.com. The destination is default-wired to the author's endpoint and is not caller-configurable in any meaningful way. The source also contains a hardcoded master-admin ID/password pair (MASTER_ADMIN_ID='15645', MASTER_ADMIN_PASS='54525645') that unconditionally returns authenticated=true, bypassing the remote auth check. package.json sets "main" to bin/index.js and the file invokes main() at the top level, so require()/import of the package also enters the interactive flow and triggers the same data submission once input is provided.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
